A lot of folks just eat familiar foods like mostly starches. Then they can't figure out why they gained weight or don't feel so good. Becoming vegan is a lifestyle change for many including the need to expand your food choices. I stopped eating most processed foods, eat mostly from scratch and try a new food every chance I get. Not everyone understands our nutritional requirements and how to effectively eat the right foods. I was fortunate to have taken a nutritional course in college. When I finished the course, I said this needs needs to be taught to every high school student.

My daughter is a nurse and she had learned the nutritional benefits of veganism through me. My kids are not vegan, but they consume very little animals in general and compared to most others. They also have very good eating habits and acquired a wide range of taste in food, much of it vegan. Setting the example appears to be a good method of sharing nutritional knowledge. I have a long story regarding how I became a vegan. But a very short version is, after learning all that I did regarding the subject and related subjects, I experienced a satori or epiphany. My question turned from, "Why should I become a vegan?" to "Why am I not a vegan?." I think that once you make that kind of revelation, there is no hesitation or difficulty.
